FOR SAL BARK

FOREWORD

Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 3 October 1972, after the draft finalized by the Tanning Materials and Allied Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. 0.2 Sal ( Shore~a robusta Gaertn.f) is a large deciduous tree, usually gregarious, growing often to a height of about 37 m and a girth of 3.7 m or In favourable localities it may attain even a height of 46 m with more. The vernacular a clean bole of 18 to 24 m and a girth of 6 to 7.5 m. names are HAL, SAL (A ssam ); SHAL (Bengali); BOLSAL, BORSAR (Garowali ); SAKHU, SAKWA, SAL, SALA ( Hindi); MULAPPUMARUTU ( Malayalam ); SAKWA ( Nepali ); SALWA, SEKWA, SORZXGHZ ( Oriya ); XUNGZLZYAM ( Tamil j and GUGAL, GUGGZLAM, SALUVA, TffAMBA, SARJAKAMU ( Telugu ). The bark of the tree is approximately 2.5 to 5.0 cm thick, rough, dark brown with conspicuous vertical cracks. Bark of young and mature trees has more tannins ( about 8 percent ) than that of the bark of old trees. The tannins are of condensed type. Normally tan/non-tan ratio ranges from 1 to 1.2. A brown dye is also sometimes extracted from the bark. Locally bast fibres are sometimes used The fibres are short, coarse and reddish in colour and for making ropes. are not of any real value. 0.3 Sal occurs widely in northern and central Region ( 1 200 to zones - one Sub-Himalayan the north of the Gangetic plain, and the other It is one of the important timber trees of Uttar Bihar, Orissa, West Bengal and Assam, besides India in apparently two 1 500 m) more or less in on the south of the Ganga. Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Nepal.

4. PACKING

AND MARKING

4.1 Packing - Unless otherwise agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier, the SAL bark shall be packed in fairly light-proof containers like gunny bags.

NOTE - The use of the IS1 Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks ) Act and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The ISI Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control ISI marked which is devised and supervised by ISI and operated by the producer. products are also continuously checked by IS1 for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the ISI Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution.

5. SAMPLING

AND CRITERIA

FOR

CONFORMITY

5.1 Scale of Sampling -Representative samples .of the material shall be drawn in accordance with Appendix A and. their conformity to the requirements of the standard shall be judged as follows. 5.2 Number of Test - Each test sample in the set shall be tested individually for all the requirements of the specification. 5.3 Criteria for Conformity - The lot shall be declared to conform to the requirements ,of this standard if each test sample in the set passes all the tests.

PREPARATION OF SAMPLES

A-2.1 Contents of each of the packages selected according to' A-L.2 and A-1.3 shall be spread upon clear; dry and level floor, so as to form a level, circular-shaped layer. Quarter the pile and repeat this process until Large pieces of bark shall be broken about 2 kg of sal bark is obtained. When it is not convenient to up before they are mixed `and quartered. spread the packages, small portions of the material shall be taken from different parts of each selected packages so as to obtain a most represenThe samples from each package shall be tative sample of the package. mixed carefully, quartered and requartered till a 2 kg sample is obtained.
*Methods of random sampling: 6

IS : 6657 - 1972 A-2.2 Test Sample - The material obtained in A-2.1 shall be divided each forming a test sample representing the into three equal parts, One set `of test sample shall be marked for the purchaser, package. another set for the supplier and the third set kept as a referee sample. A-2.2.1 All the test samples shall be immediately transferred to separate sample containers and shall be sealed air-tight and marked with full particulars necessary for proper identification, such as the name of the supplier, the place and the year of production, lot number, date of sampling, and name of material. A-2.3 Referee Sample - The referee sample shall bear the'seal of both the supplier and the purchaser and shall be kept at a place and under conditions agreed to between the two for use in case of dispute.
